scope: Proposition 4.1 of the manuscript “Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2” (preprints/Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 010 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3c8797c7d468cdcc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the tame level U2, central character ψ = χε, and full compact forms module M just defined, the following properties hold. In the second assertion weights and local parameters use the normalization of Section 2. 1. For a sufficiently small product K of uniform open subgroups of SL2(Fv), the full compact module M is finite free over O[[K]]. The integral and torsion function spaces are admissible and commute with reduction of coefficients. 2. Locally algebraic vectors are classical definite quaternionic forms of the corresponding algebraic weight. Their regular noncharacter eigenpackets transfer to Hilbert cuspidal eigenforms. They have Galois representations of determinant χ, with the local compatibility described below. 3. The regular classical vectors are dense in the Banach space. They remain dense if, at each v | 2, one fixes a smooth principal-series type with two distinct inertial characters and varies the algebraic factor with the prescribed central degree. 4. Every residual local factor T of the completed Hecke algebra away from S is a complete quotient of Rps,χ F . It is reduced and O-torsion-free, and its spectrum is the closure of its classical coefficient points.
